title: Two stacks. One path from input to output.
intro: The encoder reads the source sentence and produces contextual representations. The decoder uses those representations and earlier output tokens to predict the next token.
Follow the left encoder tower upward, cross the memory bridge, then follow the right decoder tower to the output. The moving highlight traces computation, not elapsed training.

predict.question: Where does the decoder get information about the source sentence?
options: Only from its earlier output tokens.
predict.why: Encoder output supplies the keys and values of decoder cross-attention; decoder representations supply the queries.

controls.label: Source sentence
controls.units: 0: I see cats · 1: I like cats

challenge.text: Change the source sentence from “I see cats” to “I like cats”.

figure_caption: The source token changes, encoder memory changes, and the decoder receives a different memory.

learning.objective: Locate the encoder, decoder and connection between them.
learning.action: Change the source sentence from “I see cats” to “I like cats”.
learning.observe: The source token changes, encoder memory changes, and the decoder receives a different memory.
learning.mechanism: Self-attention mixes the source representations. Cross-attention makes those encoded representations available to the decoder.

title: Words need positions before attention.
intro: Token embeddings represent token identity; sine and cosine signals add position information because the Transformer has no recurrent or convolutional sequence ordering.
The table shows the actual vectors entering the encoder. Sweep the position signal from 0% to 300%; 100% is the baseline sine/cosine encoding.

terms.definition: Source embeddings; operation from the paper, drawn schematically.
Shifted output embeddings; operation from the paper, drawn schematically.

predict.question: Why add position information?
options: Attention alone does not encode the order of the input sequence.
predict.why: The paper injects positional signals at the input because its architecture has neither recurrence nor convolution.

challenge.text: Drag position strength from 100% to 0%, then up to 300%.

figure_caption: The position contribution disappears at 0%; above 100% it becomes stronger in both stacks.

learning.objective: Separate token identity from sequence position.
learning.action: Drag position strength from 100% to 0%, then up to 300%.
learning.observe: The position contribution disappears at 0%; above 100% it becomes stronger in both stacks.
learning.mechanism: Scaled token embeddings and position vectors are added component by component before either stack.

title: Inside one encoder layer.
intro: Two projected attention heads run in parallel, their outputs are concatenated and projected, and the result passes through a residual add and layer normalization.

A position-wise feed-forward network then transforms each token separately, followed by another add and normalization. Our small model executes this entire layer; the paper stacks six. The sharpness multiplier is an illustrative intervention; 100% keeps the paper’s scaling rule.

Add & norm; operation from the paper, drawn schematically.
Encoder feed-forward; operation from the paper, drawn schematically.

predict.question: What happens after the parallel attention heads?
options: Concatenate, project, add and normalize, then apply feed-forward and another add and norm.
predict.why: Multi-head outputs are concatenated and projected. Each encoder layer includes attention and feed-forward sublayers with residual connections and normalization.

challenge.text: Sweep attention sharpness from 10% to 400%, then inspect head 2.

figure_caption: The head weight distribution changes from diffuse to concentrated; the projected values and encoder output update.

learning.objective: Trace attention, residual normalization and the feed-forward transformation.
learning.action: Sweep attention sharpness from 10% to 400%, then inspect head 2.
learning.observe: The head weight distribution changes from diffuse to concentrated; the projected values and encoder output update.
learning.mechanism: Attention exchanges information between tokens; the feed-forward network transforms each token’s features. The residual path and normalization preserve a stable route through the layer.

title: The decoder has two kinds of attention.
intro: Masked self-attention lets each output position read only its available prefix. Cross-attention separately reads the encoder’s representation of the source sentence.
The decoder inspection shows both matrices. Enable the causal mask to remove the future entries, then cut the encoder connection to see the cross-attention contribution become zero.

terms.definition: Masked self-attention; operation from the paper, drawn schematically.
Cross-attention; operation from the paper, drawn schematically.
Encoder memory; operation from the paper, drawn schematically.
Decoder feed-forward; operation from the paper, drawn schematically.

predict.question: Which connection carries the source sentence into the decoder?
predict.why: Masking restricts access within the output sequence. Cross-attention is a distinct sublayer whose keys and values come from the encoder.

challenge.text: Enable the causal mask; sweep memory contribution from 0% to 200%.

figure_caption: Future attention mass becomes exactly zero. Cutting memory makes the cross-attention output zero, while the decoder still has its prefix.

learning.objective: Distinguish decoder masking from access to the source.
learning.action: Enable the causal mask; sweep memory contribution from 0% to 200%.
learning.observe: Future attention mass becomes exactly zero. Cutting memory makes the cross-attention output zero, while the decoder still has its prefix.
learning.mechanism: The mask excludes future logits before softmax. Cross-attention uses decoder queries and encoder keys/values; zero memory has zero value contribution.

title: Predict a token. Feed it back. Repeat.
intro: A linear projection maps decoder features into vocabulary logits; softmax turns those logits into next-token probabilities. Greedy decoding selects the highest-probability token.
Generate up to twelve tokens. Each selected token is appended to the decoder prefix and used by the next pass. Fixed, untrained weights produce token IDs, not a meaningful translation.

Linear & softmax; operation from the paper, drawn schematically.

Shifted output embeddings; operation from the paper, drawn schematically.

predict.question: What is fed into the next decoding pass?
options: The previously generated tokens, shifted after the start token.
predict.why: Autoregressive generation conditions each next prediction on the source and previously generated outputs.

challenge.text: Generate from one to twelve tokens and follow the growing decoder prefix.

figure_caption: The generated sequence grows, the shifted prefix includes earlier generated tokens, and the probability distribution is recomputed.

learning.objective: Follow autoregressive feedback from probability to the next decoder input.
learning.action: Generate from one to twelve tokens and follow the growing decoder prefix.
learning.observe: The generated sequence grows, the shifted prefix includes earlier generated tokens, and the probability distribution is recomputed.
learning.mechanism: The encoder memory can be reused, but the decoder runs again with the growing prefix. Future tokens are unavailable when each prediction is made.

title: What was trained—and what this demo proves.
intro: The paper trains with Adam, learning-rate warmup, dropout and label smoothing. Its reported translation benchmarks and ablations are evidence from trained models, not consequences of a diagram.

The schedule below is equation (3), using the paper’s model dimension and 4,000 warmup steps. The evidence panel separately cites translation results, computational comparisons, parsing and limitations.

predict.question: Does this small untrained model reproduce the paper’s translation scores?
options: No; those are reported results of the paper’s trained models.
Yes, because its weights sum to one.
predict.why: Numerical architecture checks establish implementation behavior. Translation benchmarks require trained models, data, evaluation and compute described in the paper.

challenge.text: Sweep the schedule from step 1 through warmup at 4,000 to step 32,000.

figure_caption: The learning rate falls after warmup. The reported BLEU scores stay in the evidence panel because this demo does not train or measure translation quality.

learning.objective: Distinguish a reproducible mechanism from a published empirical result.
learning.action: Sweep the schedule from step 1 through warmup at 4,000 to step 32,000.
learning.observe: The learning rate falls after warmup. The reported BLEU scores stay in the evidence panel because this demo does not train or measure translation quality.
learning.mechanism: After warmup, equation (3) decays as the inverse square root of the step. Source results, measured demo checks and omitted experiments are kept separate.
